lines.trans: Look at page one, Rami: conversion to commercial offices next month. We are finished!
Be patient, sir, did you read the second page clipped underneath it?
Only small grey numbers! My heart stopped at page one!
Look where Rami is pointing with the pencil, Mr Mazen!
Clause fourteen of the Amman Old Quarter Act, and my brother here just nodded!

No courtyard building over eighty years old may become private offices if the ground floor serves neighbours daily.
Serves neighbours daily... like a morning café open to the public?!

Wait, if we open the courtyard gate every morning for neighbours' coffee and bread...
Then your lease is protected for ten more years by city law!

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb for 'to see, look, check' (بشوف / شاف).

examples.trans: Look inside the suitcase, Nour!
I will see you tomorrow at breakfast.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: صفحات.

examples.trans: Read the second page of the letter.
The notebook fell open to the middle page.

meanings.note: Before an indefinite noun أول means 'first' (أول يوم 'first day'); after a definite noun الأول / الأولى agrees in gender (الصفحة الأولى 'the first page'). Also used adverbially ('first').

examples.trans: Welcome on your first day of work!
Read the first page calmly.

meanings.note: Placed directly before a name or title when addressing someone in Arabic (يا نور 'Nour!', يا أستاذ 'sir!') and in exclamations (يا سلام! 'wonderful!').

examples.trans: Good morning, Tariq!
Oh, how lovely the sun is after the rain!

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: تحويلات.

examples.trans: Converting the building into offices is prohibited.
We read the conversion request in the morning.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: مكاتب.

examples.trans: The keys are on the reception desk.
The wooden desk under the window is wide.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: تجارية, plural: تجاريين).

examples.trans: Converting the house into commercial offices is forbidden.
This is a residential street, not commercial.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: شهور.

examples.trans: That was the best sleep in a month!
The contract renews at the start of next month.

meanings.note: Active participle of إجا ('to come'): means 'on the way / arriving' (جايين 'they are coming') and after a time noun 'next' (الأسبوع الجاي 'next week').

examples.trans: The guests are coming down the stairs now.
We will see you next week!

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بنتهي, بينتهي).

examples.trans: The problem ended well.
We thought everything was over.

meanings.note: Before a time noun, طول (tuul) means 'all ... long / throughout' (طول الليل all night long, طول الأسبوع all week).

examples.trans: The rain fell all night long.
Breakfast is free all week long.

meanings.note: Used in core Jordanian idioms like طول بالك ('be patient'), هدي بالك ('calm down'), and جاي على بالي ('I feel like').

examples.trans: Be patient a moment, everything is fine.

examples.text: جاي على بالي كاسة شاي بالنعنع.
examples.trans: I feel like having a glass of mint tea.

meanings.note: Polite Jordanian title for any man ('sir / Mr') as well as 'teacher' or 'professor'.

examples.trans: Please have a seat, sir.
Good morning, gentlemen.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بقرأ, بيقرأ).

examples.trans: I want to read the booking ledger.
Did you read the second page clipped underneath?

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: تانية, plural: تانيين).

examples.trans: Room four is on the second floor.
There is a second sheet behind the letter.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: مشبوكة, plural: مشبوكين).

examples.text: في صفحة تانية مشبوكة ورا الرسالة.
examples.trans: There is a second page clipped behind the letter.
The lamp is plugged in.

meanings.note: Used both before a noun ('under, beneath') and standalone ('downstairs').

examples.trans: Let us bring it downstairs into the light.
The wide desk is under the window.

meanings.note: Extremely common Jordanian word meaning both 'only / just' (بس نص كاسة 'just half a glass') and 'but' between clauses.

examples.text: بدي أقرأ الدفتر، بس مش ملاقي نظارتي!
examples.trans: I want to read the ledger, only I cannot find my glasses!
Just half a glass, please.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: أرقام.

examples.trans: Here is your key, room number four.
Is there a phone number written on the paper?

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: رمادية, plural: رماديين).

examples.trans: He is wearing a dark grey coat.

examples.text: بدنا نحمي بيتنا من المكاتب الرمادية.
examples.trans: We want to protect our house from grey offices.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: صغيرة, plural: صغار).

examples.trans: We found a little wooden train in the bag.
There are two small streets on the left.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: قلوب.

examples.trans: My heart is beating fast with joy!
Welcome from the bottom of my heart.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بوقف, بيوقف).

examples.trans: A yellow taxi stopped outside the gate!
My heart stopped at page one!

meanings.note: Marks location ('at, by') and with pronoun suffixes expresses possession: عندي ('I have'), عندك ('you have'), عندنا ('we have').

examples.trans: A taxi just stopped at the door.
I have a reservation under the name Suad.

meanings.note: Form II طلّع means both 'look!' (طلّع بالمراية) and 'bring/carry up' (رح أطلّع الشنتة).

examples.text: طلع بالمراية ورا المكتب يا معلم!
examples.trans: Look in the mirror behind the desk, boss!
I will carry the blue suitcase up for you.

meanings.note: Spoken Jordanian question word for 'where?'.

examples.trans: Where is the computer, Tariq?
Where should I put the small spoons?

meanings.note: Levantine progressive marker placed before a present-tense verb to show action happening right now.

examples.trans: The water is flowing inside the pipe right now!

examples.text: كنت عم بدور على دفتري هلا.
examples.trans: I was just looking for my notebook.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بأشر, بيأشر).

examples.trans: Salma motioned to me from the kitchen.
Rami is pointing to the two chairs.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: أقلام.

examples.trans: I found my pen in the jacket pocket.
We write the names with a pencil.

meanings.note: Paired with قلم in قلم رصاص ('pencil').

examples.trans: We write bookings in pencil.
The name is written in pencil underneath.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: بنود.

examples.trans: Read clause four in the contract.
This clause protects the tenant.

meanings.note: Spoken Jordanian numeral 'fourteen'.

examples.trans: What does clause fourteen say?
It is seven fourteen.

meanings.note: Everyday preposition meaning 'from', 'of', or 'than' after comparatives.

examples.trans: I am Salma from the kitchen.
Breakfast is from seven-thirty to ten.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: قوانين.

examples.trans: Heritage law protects historic houses.
Rami knows building regulations well.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: أحياء.

examples.trans: The old quarter in Amman is calm and beautiful.
The district law protects courtyards.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: قديمة, plural: قدام).

examples.trans: The courtyard has an old jasmine tree.
The old hardware shop is past the bridge.

meanings.note: Takes a long -uu-/-oo- stem with possessive endings in Jordanian (أخوي my brother, أخوك your brother); dual أخوين.

examples.trans: My older brother lives in Amman.
The brothers sat together in the courtyard.

meanings.note: Used both before a noun ('outside the gate') and standalone ('outside').

examples.trans: It is raining outside.
A yellow taxi stopped outside the gate.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بهز, بيهز).

examples.trans: My brother nodded his head in agreement!
The breeze shook the jasmine branches.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: روس.

examples.trans: My glasses were on my head!

examples.text: انتبه على راسك من السقف الواطي.
examples.trans: Watch your head on the low ceiling.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: موافقات.

examples.trans: He nodded his head in agreement with a smile.
We received official municipal approval.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun.

examples.trans: Explain the matter to me in plain words.
Your words are kind and reassuring.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: بسيطة, plural: بسيطين).

examples.trans: Explain the matter to me in simple words.
The problem is minor and easy to fix.

meanings.note: Used mainly in polite/earnest requests: أرجوك (to a man), أرجوكي (to a woman), أرجوكم (plural) — 'please!'.

examples.trans: Please write down that sentence!
Please do not open the white parcel.

meanings.note: Signature Levantine question word for 'what?'.

examples.trans: What is that sound?
What is written on the sheet, Rami?

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بقول, بيقول).

examples.trans: What does clause fourteen say?
He said thank you and hung up!

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: ممنوعة, plural: ممنوعين).

examples.trans: Converting heritage houses into offices is prohibited.
Noise is not allowed after ten o'clock.

meanings.note: In questions أي means 'which?' (أي علبة؟ 'which tin?'); in conditionals/negatives it means 'any' (أي شي 'anything').

examples.trans: Which tub of butter did you bring?

examples.text: رني الجرس إذا احتجتي أي شي.
examples.trans: Ring the bell if you need anything.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: بنايات.

examples.trans: The stone building is eighty years old.
The building owner sent a letter.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: ساحات.

examples.trans: The courtyard has a big jasmine tree.
We sat drinking tea in the courtyard.

meanings.note: Arabic expresses age with عمر + possessive suffix: عمره تمانين سنة ('its/his age is eighty years').

examples.trans: The building is eighty years old.
He has lived in this quarter all his life.

meanings.note: Used both before a noun ('above, over') and standalone ('upstairs').

examples.trans: The window is above the old tree.
Let us go upstairs to see the room.

meanings.note: Spoken Jordanian numeral 'eighty'.

examples.text: خشب بلوط أصلي عمره تمانين سنة.
examples.trans: Solid oak wood eighty years old.
This house has lived through eighty winters!

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: سنين.

examples.trans: The building is eighty years old.
I have not seen him for three years.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: خاصة, plural: خاصين).

examples.trans: Converting the house into private offices is forbidden.

examples.text: هادي وصفة خاصة من مطبخ سلمى.
examples.trans: This is a special recipe from Salma's kitchen.

meanings.note: Everyday conditional word 'if' for real possibilities.

examples.text: رني الجرس إذا احتجتي أي شي.
examples.trans: Ring the bell if you need anything.

examples.text: إذا فتحنا الساحة الصبح، الجيران بيفرحوا.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: طوابق.

examples.trans: Your room is on the second floor on the right.
The building has three storeys.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: أرضية, plural: أرضيين).

examples.trans: The kitchen is on the ground floor.
The ground-floor rooms are close to the courtyard.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بخدم, بيخدم).

examples.trans: The tables serve the neighbours every day.
We served the neighbourhood for fifteen years.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: جيران.

examples.trans: All the neighbours on the street are kind.
Good morning, dear neighbour.

meanings.note: Adverb 'on a daily basis, every day'.

examples.trans: The ground floor serves the neighbours daily.
We bake fresh bread daily.

meanings.note: Spoken Levantine form of مثل ('like, similar to').

examples.trans: Its color is dark blue like your suitcase!
The water is cold as ice.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: كافيهات.

examples.trans: We opened a small café in the house courtyard.
The morning café serves all the neighbours.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: صباحية, plural: صباحيين).

I love morning coffee in the courtyard.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: مفتوحة, plural: مفتوحين).

examples.trans: Is the hardware shop open right now?
Here is to neighbours and our open gates!

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: ناس.

examples.trans: You are kind, generous people.
Morning coffee brings people together in the courtyard.

meanings.note: Signature Jordanian/Palestinian pronunciation (with z) of بالضبط ('exactly!').

examples.trans: Exactly! You have become one of us.
Tell me exactly what to buy.

meanings.note: Adverb 'at the moment, for now'.

examples.trans: For now, the suitcase is safe and sound in the closet.
Currently the tables serve the inn's guests.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: طاولات.

examples.trans: We set four tables in the courtyard.
Breakfast is ready on the table.

meanings.note: Numeral 'four'; short form أربع (arba') directly before a plural noun (أربع طاولات 'four tables').

examples.trans: Room four is arriving today.
Four tables and eight chairs in the courtyard.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: ضيوف.

examples.trans: The guests are coming down to breakfast now.
We welcomed every guest with a smile.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: نزل.

examples.text: نزل الساحة فيه تمن غرف هادية.
examples.trans: The courtyard guesthouse has eight quiet rooms.
Welcome to our small guesthouse.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: لحظات.

examples.trans: Wait a moment, let me read the line.
We waited a moment by the gate.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بفتح, بيفتح).

examples.trans: The corner shop opens at seven.
Oh, the door finally opened!

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: بوابات.

examples.trans: The courtyard gate is open for guests.
The taxi stopped outside the gate.

meanings.note: Before an indefinite singular noun كل means 'every' (كل يوم 'every day'); before a definite noun it means 'all / the whole' (كل الأسبوع 'all week').

examples.trans: Tell me everything I need to know.
Everyone is happy in the courtyard today.

meanings.note: Everyday spoken Jordanian noun for 'the morning' (الصبح in the morning, كل صبح every morning).

examples.trans: I drink black coffee every morning.
The morning bread is still hot.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: قهاوي.

examples.text: بتحبي قهوة مع هيل ولا شاي؟
examples.trans: Would you like cardamom coffee or tea?
Morning coffee is ready on the stove.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: خبزات.

examples.trans: The morning bread is fresh and hot.
We ate bread with cheese and olives.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: أوقات.

examples.trans: Old pipes take time to warm up.
You arrived right on time.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: عقود.

examples.trans: The lease contract is protected by law.
He works at the municipal contracts office.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: إيجارات.

examples.trans: The shop rent is paid until summer.
We signed the lease today.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: محمية, plural: محميين).

examples.trans: Your lease is protected by city law!
The courtyard is sheltered from street wind.

meanings.note: Numeral 'ten'; short form عشر ('ashar) before a plural noun (عشر دقايق 'ten minutes').

examples.trans: You arrived ten minutes early.
Breakfast is from seven-thirty to ten.

كمان.gloss: also; too; again (كمان مرة once more)

meanings.en: also; too; again (كمان مرة once more)
meanings.note: Everyday Levantine word for 'also, too, more' (كمان مرة 'one more time / again').

examples.text: التفكير السريع أنقذ الفطور كمان مرة!
examples.trans: Quick thinking saved breakfast once again!
And I missed you too.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: مدن.

examples.trans: Amman is an old, lovely hilltop city.
City law protects public gardens.

meanings.note: Singular نظارة means one pair of glasses in Arabic (نظارتي my glasses); dual نظارتين means two pairs of glasses!

examples.trans: I cannot find my glasses on the desk!
He pulled his glasses down off his forehead and laughed.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بوقع, بيوقع).

examples.text: نظارتك وقعت عن أنفك من الفرحة!
examples.trans: Your glasses fell off your nose for joy!

examples.text: أي نزل سحري هاد اللي وقعت فيه؟
examples.trans: What magical inn is this that you stumbled into?

meanings.note: Means 'about' (عن الزبدة), 'off / away from' (عن جبيني), and appears in عن جد ('really!') and عن إذنك ('excuse me').

examples.trans: I will carry the suitcase up for you.
I heard your voices about the butter!

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: أنوف.

examples.trans: Your glasses are on your nose now.
The air feels cold on my nose in the morning.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: فرحات.

examples.trans: His eyes shone with joy!
The family's joy is beyond words.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: مرات.

examples.trans: The doorbell rang twice.
I read the letter three times.

meanings.note: Everyday preposition 'with'; takes pronoun suffixes to express 'have on one's person' (معي 'I have with me', معك حق 'you are right').

examples.trans: You are right, Nour!
Goodbye! (lit. go with safety)

meanings.note: Core word in مع السلامة! ('goodbye!', literally 'with safety') and الحمد لله عالسلامة ('glad you arrived safely').

examples.trans: Goodbye, see you tomorrow!
Thank goodness for your safe arrival.

meanings.note: Ordinal number from أربعة (four). Feminine: رابعة.

examples.text: البند الرابع عشر من قانون عمان القديمة.
examples.trans: Clause fourteen of the Amman Old Quarter Act.
This is the fourth cup of coffee today.

meanings.note: Invariant spoken Jordanian relative pronoun ('who, which, that') for any gender or number.

examples.trans: That is what I want.
The inn that keeps a stranger's bag safe.

meanings.note: Spoken Jordanian/Levantine word for 'here' (لهون 'to here', من هون 'from here').

examples.trans: Here we use this big ledger.
Stay right here a minute.

meanings.note: Warm spoken Levantine affirmative particle alongside آه and نعم.

examples.trans: He nodded his head yes.
Yes indeed, you are right.
